label: prop:binding-genfun-qdifference
title: The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence
html:
Proposition (q-difference recurrence of the binding generating function; conditional on conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration).

Let G(x;q)=\sum_{n\geq 0} B_n(K)\,x^n be the generating function of the body-order binding terms (conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration). Suppose G satisfies a fibre-level q-difference equation

G(qx;q) \;=\; R(q,x)\,G(x;q),
\qquad R(q,x)\in\mathbb{Q}(q)[x,x^{-1}]\ \text{of bounded depth }d .

Then:

  1. Linear recurrence. The body terms satisfy a depth-d linear recurrence B_{n+d} = \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} a_j(q)\,B_{n+j}, with kernel \{a_j\} read off from R. In particular the empirical "\rho\cdot A" scale rule governing the growth of the terms is the solution of the recurrence — an output of R, not a fitted constant.
  2. Archimedean image. Under the realisation functor \tau at q=q_0, the q-difference equation passes to a linear (Dirac-type) differential equation on the realised generating function: the fibre q-shift becomes a derivation in the archimedean limit.

The implications (1)--(2) are the standard passage from a q-holonomic generating function to a P-recursive coefficient sequence and its confluent (differential) limit; they hold for any such R. What is open is the existence and identity of the kernel R for the binding G. By the precision-floor obstruction — the c_k information bound, which makes term data unmeasurable beyond low order — R cannot be fixed by fitting the B_n; it must be derived from the fibre root-of-unity singularity structure of the Seiberg--Witten differential (prop:sw-period-residue-sum). This is the same q-difference machinery as the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder, applied to the binding series.

Scope note (2026-08-26) — the rank-1 hypothesis is unsatisfiable on both proposed carriers; the proposition survives only in rank 2. The supposition above is a first-order (rank-1) q-difference relation. Two carriers have been proposed for G, and neither admits one.

The raw carrier — the ordinary generating function of the raw body terms B_n = I(n)/n — was excluded by the confluent/Gevrey growth argument (QOU.Mass.QDifferenceConfluentObstruction.no_bounded_depth_first_order_kernel, sorry-free). That exclusion explicitly re-targeted the conjecture at the q-Borel / Gevrey-normalized carrier b_n = f_n/[n]_q!, predicting depth d = 2. The normalized carrier provably satisfies [m+2]_q\,b_{m+2} = b_{m+1} + b_m, i.e. the operator L_{\mathcal{K}} = (q^2x-1)\sigma^2 - (q-1)\sigma - (q-1) named by conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol.

A scalar kernel is a first-order right factor \sigma - a of L_{\mathcal{K}}, i.e. a solution a\in K(x) of the q-Riccati equation (q^2x-1)\,a(qx)\,a(x) - (q-1)\,a(x) - (q-1) = 0. Writing a = P/Q and clearing denominators, the three terms have degrees 1+2p, p+u and 2u with p = \deg P, u = \deg Q. The first is odd-shaped and the third even, so 1+2p = 2u is impossible over \mathbb{Z}; a two-line case split then gives that the maximum is attained exactly once for every (p,u), and a lone top-degree term cannot cancel. Hence no rational a exists, \mathcal{K} is irreducible of rank 2, and no nonzero solution of L_{\mathcal{K}} obeys any scalar relation G(qx) = R(q,x)G(x) with R \in K(x) — a fortiori none with R\in\mathbb{Q}(q)[x,x^{-1}] of any depth d; the depth never enters the argument, only the degrees do. Sorry-free in QOU.Mass.BindingScalarKernelParityExclusion.

Scope (b), structural exclusion, invariant cited. The parity is the Newton-slope invariant: L_{\mathcal{K}} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12 at infinity, every rank-1 q-difference module has integer slope, and Newton slopes are additive on sub- and quotient modules. Independently corroborated by the van der Put--Reversat classification of pure modules [vanderput-reversat2007, vanderput2006]: a pure module of non-integral slope d/r, \gcd(d,r)=1, and rank r is E(r,d,b) in Bugeaud's notation [bugeaud2011], and it is irreducible.

What survives. Implications (1)--(2) are unaffected and the depth-2 prediction stands — but depth 2 means rank 2: the kernel is a 2\times2 matrix A(q,x) acting on (G, \sigma G), whose \tau-image is a first-order two-component system, which is what "Dirac-type" already asks for. Restated in rank 2 the proposition is intact; restated in rank 1 it is vacuous. The exclusion is over K(x): after a degree-2 ramified base change (adjoining q^{1/2}, x^{1/2}) the slope becomes the integer 1 and a scalar kernel does exist on the double cover, relating half-shifts — that is, even and odd body orders separately. That ramification is the missing structure, not a gap in the argument.
